earlier_scan.source_named: Lynch & Crowley 2001 (Languages of Vanuatu) list Baetora as essentially undescribed; no grammar or phonology located.

sources.citation: ABVD: Baetora (Nasawa), language id 1067 (source Tryon 1976; Glottocode nasa1241), https://abvd.eva.mpg.de/austronesian/language.php?id=1067
sources.note: 147 items retyped from Tryon 1976; no stress marks, no notes on stress.

sources.citation: Codrington, R. H. 1885. The Melanesian languages. Oxford: Clarendon. Ch. 16 'Maewo, Aurora Island', pp. 408-420 (Tanoriki, north Maewo).
sources.note: archive.org djvu text scanned in the Maewo grammar (Tanoriki = Sungwadia, north Maewo, not Baetora) contains no accent statement; the accent remarks retrieved ('It cannot be said that the accent usually falls on any one syllable, except in words of two syllables, in which the stress is on the first') belong to the Mota grammar.

sources.citation: Rangelov, Tihomir, Eleanor Ridge & Lana Takau. 2025. Linguistics in Vanuatu 45 years after Independence. Te Reo 68(2): 31-78.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Appendix table row 46: 'Baetora baet1237 No grammar / Short list / 0.0 / No corpus / Bible parts'; text: 'Maewo's three languages score quite poorly, except for one full grammar' (that grammar is Henri 2011 for Sungwadia, not Baetora).

sources.citation: Walworth, Mary, Amy Dewar, Thomas Ennever, Lana Takau & Iveth Rodriguez. 2021. Multilingualism in Vanuatu: four case studies. International Journal of Bilingualism (doi:10.1177/13670069211023132), Maewo section pp. 14-16.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or phonology. 2018 survey found 'at least eight autochthonous languages and 19 different language varieties' on Maewo; the Baetora (btr) area corresponds to Sungwaloge (Tawet, Sungwadola/Sungwadoga), Nalemba (Nasawa, Narovorovo) and Xalangi (Baetora village) varieties, plus moribund Sungagage in the south.

sources.citation: Shimelman, Aviva, Paul Heggarty, Lana Takau, Mary Walworth, Tom Ennever, Iveth Rodriguez et al. 2019-. Vanuatu Voices (Sound Comparisons Vanuatu), CLDF dataset lexibank/vanuatuvoices; https://vanuatuvoices.clld.org. Maewo recordings and transcriptions by Ennever & Rodriguez (2018).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonetic wordlists (2,204 forms) for 11 btr-coded doculects (Tawet: Naviso; Nalemba: Narovorovo, Nasawa; Sungwadoga: Rata; Sungwadola: Gwaran Uta; Tawet: Narovorovo; Xalangi: Baetora; Sungagage x3; Raga: Avavanvae) with audio, but stress is not transcribed (a single stress mark in the whole 45,255-row dataset, in a Santo language). No statement.

sources.citation: Clark, Ross. 2009. *Leo Tuai: a comparative lexical study of North and Central Vanuatu languages. Pacific Linguistics 603. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 C59 2009
sources.note: Baetora is a 'core language' of the lexical corpus but is not one of the 15 sample languages with a phonology sketch; no Baetora stress statement. Only a proto-level inference, 2.1.3 p. 16: 'Word stress in PNCV was most likely on the penultimate vowel. This is its position in almost all daughter languages for which phonological descriptions exist, where the historic final syllable is intact.'

sources.citation: Lynch, John & Terry Crowley. 2001. Languages of Vanuatu: a new survey and bibliography. Pacific Linguistics 517. Canberra: ANU. Section 3.5.3 Baetora, p. 63; summary table 3.5.5.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 L96 2001)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6211.V36 L96 2001
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States that the only knowledge of Baetora is Tryon's (1976) five wordlists (Nasawa, Navenevene, Tam, Narovorovo, Baetora); summary table: Phonology 'no', Grammar 'no', Lexicon 'brief'. Gives two dialects (Tawet, Surtas) per C. Hyslop p.c.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. 1976. New Hebrides languages: an internal classification. Pacific Linguistics C-50. Canberra: ANU. (Baetora-area wordlists nos. 20-24: Navenevene, Tam, Nasawa, Narovorovo, Baetora.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number PL6211.N44 T7
sources.note: No stress statement for any Maewo language and no stress marks in the wordlists. p. 74: 'The transcription of items listed in the Appendix is a broad phonetic transcription. No attempt at phonemic analysis has been made'. Only comparative note (p. 66): 'Considerable dialect variation has been noted in this south-central Maewo language, each village recognisably different from the other.'

sources.citation: Any future grammar/phonology of Sungwaloge/Nalemba/Xalangi (Baetora) from the MPI-EVA Maewo team (Ennever, Rodriguez, Walworth) — none published as of Rangelov, Ridge & Takau 2025.

sources.note: The 2018 survey team is the only group with recent field data; a sketch from them would be the first description. Nothing located by web search in 2026.

sources.citation: Ennever, Thomas & Iveth Rodriguez. 2019. Survey of languages spoken on Maewo (IRTE1). PARADISEC. Audio wordlists (ABVD 215 items), kinship surveys, interviews from Maewo villages incl. Baetora-area villages.

sources.note: Only recorded primary data with audio for Baetora varieties (Nasawa, Narovorovo, Navenevene, Naviso, Baetora village); stress could be determined from the recordings, though no written statement is expected. Vanuatu Voices audio (open) derives from this fieldwork.

sources.citation: Henri, Agnès. 2011. Le sungwadia: éléments de description d'une langue du Vanuatu. Leuven: Peeters (Linguistique de la SLP 97). Based on 2010 Paris-4 thesis.

sources.note: Full grammar of Sungwadia (mari1426, north Maewo); would give the only documented stress pattern for a Maewo language, as an areal proxy only — not a Baetora statement.

sources.citation: Ivens, W. G. 1940. A grammar of the language of Lotora, Maewo, New Hebrides, Melanesia. Bulletin of SOAS 10(3): 679-698.

sources.note: The only older grammar of a Maewo language beyond Codrington; NOT Baetora (Lotora = Sungwadia per Lynch & Crowley 2001:62, or Sungwadaga per Wikipedia) but the closest neighbouring description; may contain an accent note usable as an areal proxy.
